title: He lost his hand to a falling metal sheet in 2015. He won Paralympic bronze in javelin twice. October 11, 2026.
excerpt: From a freedom-struggle leader born on a river island, to a physician who traded a US career for one of India's most overlooked regions, October 11's five stories are about rebuilding after something broke, not avoiding the break in the first place.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about continuing after a real setback - a philosophy of grassroots democracy that outlasted the man who championed it, a genetic discovery that turned a guessing-game disease into a treatable one, a medical career rebuilt in a village instead of a hospital system, a patrol ship that's one of a sustained production line rather than a one-off, and an athlete who kept throwing javelin after losing a hand and being disqualified from an Olympics.

October 11, 1902: a boy was born in a river-island village who would spend his life arguing for power to stay close to the people

Jayaprakash Narayan was born in Sitab Diara on the Ganga, drawn early to the Sarvodaya philosophy of Gandhi and Vinoba Bhave. Known as 'JP' or 'Lok Nayak,' he championed grassroots self-governance and civil liberties for decades, earning a posthumous Bharat Ratna in 1999.

He found the genetic switch behind the most common prostate cancer mutation. It just won him medicine's Harrington Prize

Dr. Arul M. Chinnaiyan, a second-generation Indian-American at the University of Michigan, won the 2026 International Harrington Prize for discovering the TMPRSS2-ERG gene fusion - the most common genetic alteration in prostate cancer, and research that helped identify which mutations respond to specific drugs.

She gave up a pediatrics career in the US to build a hospital for one of India's most overlooked regions

Dr. Lata Desai trained in medicine in Gujarat, specialized in pediatrics in the US, then returned to found SEWA Rural in 1980 in tribal Bharuch district - four decades of grassroots health work that earned her the Padma Shri in 2022.

India's Coast Guard just commissioned a patrol ship with a feature no Indian vessel of its class had before

ICGS Ajit, an indigenous Fast Patrol Vessel with twin engines driving controllable pitch propellers, was commissioned October 9, 2026, at Goa Shipyard Limited with over 65% indigenous content - the latest in a sustained production line, not a single ceremonial build.

He lost his hand to a falling metal sheet in 2015. He won Paralympic bronze in javelin twice

Sundar Singh Gurjar lost his hand in an accident, rebuilt his javelin career in the F46 para-athletics classification, survived a devastating disqualification at the Rio 2016 Paralympics, and went on to win two World Championship golds and bronze medals at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Paralympics.

Five stories, one thread: a philosophy that outlived its champion, a discovery that replaced guesswork with precision, a career rebuilt in a village instead of a hospital system, a ship that's part of a pattern instead of an exception, and an athlete who kept throwing after losing a hand and an Olympic shot both. None of it stayed broken.
